prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "imagerender", with the standing line "Turns every diagram, chart, and illustration source an essay calls for into a PNG, repairing broken sources and retrying." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows At left, an essay's image folder holds three source files, each tagged by a small card. Each file travels its own track rightward through a gate, then into its renderer. The mermaid file enters the Mermaid renderer with its theme file. The R file enters an R script run fed by common.R. The prompt file enters the image model. Each track exits right as a PNG. Beneath the mermaid and r tracks, a return arc leaves each failed render carrying error output and source up to the writing model. The repaired source is written back into the same file, and the arc re-enters the renderer, marked with three tick marks. The ai track has its own short loop: a rejected prompt is rewritten once, then retried.

Magnified circles set beside it show The first circle shows two file clocks compared; a PNG newer than its source is skipped, and --force forces it open. The second shows error output and source travelling together to the writing model, with fixed code returning. The third shows a JPEG reply re-encoded into a PNG inside a landscape 3:2 frame. In the row of studies, one study shows a meta card with three fields, and another shows repair calls entering a cost ledger.

Colour is used so that Rust marks failure and every repair or rewrite path. Teal marks the successful path to a finished PNG. Grey marks the placeholder stand-in.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 3 methods, drawn as three tracks; up to 3 repair rounds, drawn as three ticks on the return arc; 1 safety rewrite on the ai loop; 3:2 landscape frame for drawn figures; 3 closing tallies of rendered, skipped, and failed.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: .meta.yaml on the tag card; filename, method, and description as its fields; mermaid, r, and ai on the three tracks; figure.mermaid, figure.R, and figure.ai-prompt.txt on the source files; common.R feeding the R run; --force on the gate; slug on the essay folder; PNG on each output; placeholder on the grey stand-in; cost ledger beside the writing model; cheap and pro as the model tiers; rendered, skipped, and failed on the closing tally.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: figure.mermaid, figure.R, figure.ai-prompt.txt, Mermaid theme, common.R, image model, writing model, repaired source, retry, safety rewrite; stale or fresh, --force, error output, JPEG to PNG, landscape 3:2; .meta.yaml, filename, method, description, cost ledger; PNG, grey placeholder, rendered, skipped, failed; every slug, one slug only, cheap, pro

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Broken sources go back for repair; Repaired source overwrites the original file. PNG newer than source is skipped; Every figure is stored as PNG. Method names which source file to read; Every repair call is recorded. Placeholder bears the prompt text, visibly. Walks every essay, or just one.
